members.tone: The plain term of the set, naming the feeling of well-being itself without saying whether it is quiet or loud.
French, and it bundles good humor in with the happiness where *happiness* names the feeling alone.
Joy and pleasure actively felt rather than merely possessed, warmer than *contentment* and quieter than *merriment*.
The same joy and pleasure as *gladness*, given a fuller and more formal shape.
Literary in cast, dressing the joy and pleasure of *gladness* in ornament the plainer form does without.
Brightness and lightness in the feeling, weightless where *rejoicing* is full and heavy.
The same gay feeling with an outward, jolly noise on it that *gaiety* need not have.
The peak of the set, happiness raised to great intensity rather than left at an even glow.
Pins the happiness to a secure relationship rather than leaving it a free-floating mood as *gladness* does.
Good spirits that rise unbidden, a steady sunniness rather than the crest of *rejoicing*.
The same spontaneous good spirits with a lighter, more carefree edge than *cheerfulness*.
The quietest member, happiness settled on one's situation in life instead of flaring at anything in particular.
